$comment: Active catalog. It contains real engines only — there are no mock entries and nothing here is synthetic. Adding a model means editing this file: copy the host and model entries you run from config/examples/real-models.example.json, adjust them, and restart DSH. No code changes are needed for any engine whose adapter kind is already registered. See docs/adding-a-model.md. This machine opted into hub-managed process launching (the profile patch sets allowProcessLaunch: true), so the comfyui host declares a lifecycle and can be cold-started and stopped on demand; the ollama host stays startable:false, because its service is managed outside the hub.

hosts.$comment: Ollama runs as a background service you manage. `ollama serve` owns port 11434, and every pulled model is reachable through the same OpenAI-compatible surface. Set startable/stoppable to true and add a `start` command if you want the hub to launch it for you.
hosts.name: Ollama
hosts.notes: External process. The hub only ever probes /api/tags and posts to /v1/chat/completions.

hosts.$comment: ComfyUI has a graph API rather than a prompt endpoint, so it has its own `comfyui` adapter. A model points at a template with `adapterConfig.workflowPath`; the adapter writes the prompt into the CLIPTextEncode node wired to the sampler's `positive` link, queues the graph, polls /history, and downloads from /view.
hosts.name: ComfyUI
hosts.notes: Startable on this machine: `invoke_model` cold-starts ComfyUI when it is down, `start_model` starts it explicitly, and `stop_model` releases its VRAM afterwards. The command is this install's own launcher — C:/ComfyUI/venv/Scripts/python.exe running src/main.py from C:/ComfyUI/src, which is where the venv's relative paths and the install log expect it to run from. `--lowvram` is required here, not a preference: the GPU has 8 GB and the Z-Image Turbo graph stages about 5.9 GB, which the default mode OOMs on. `startupTimeoutMs: 300000` is deliberate — loading the checkpoint and the text encoder genuinely takes minutes on this hardware, so a shorter budget would abort a start that was going to succeed. `awaitHealthOnStart: true` is what keeps `start_model` and a cold `invoke_model` from returning before /system_stats answers. Set startable/stoppable back to false (or override this row in your profile's cordis.patch.yml) if the engine should be managed by hand, and remember the deployment must also set allowProcessLaunch: true — a startable descriptor alone launches nothing.

models.$comment: A generic starter. `adapterConfig.model` is the name Ollama knows the checkpoint by, so point it at something you have actually pulled: `ollama list` shows the names, `ollama pull llama3.2` gets this one.
models.name: Ollama text model
models.notes: Rename this to the checkpoint you run, or add one entry per checkpoint — several models may share the `ollama` host.

models.$comment: The template in config/workflows/ was captured from a real run. Z-Image Turbo is step-distilled: 8 steps at cfg 1.0 is its intended operating point. A relative `workflowPath` is relative to the catalog that writes it, and this catalog lives in `config/` — so `workflows/z-image-turbo.api.json` means `config/workflows/z-image-turbo.api.json`. Writing `config/workflows/…` here would compose to `config/config/workflows/…`, which has never existed.
models.name: Z-Image Turbo (ComfyUI)
models.notes: The template names the checkpoint, text encoder and VAE, so those files must exist in your ComfyUI models directory. Delete this entry if you do not run ComfyUI.
